params.name: q
params.resample_while: q == p or (p + q) % 2 == 1 or p + q > 280

stem: $ABCD$ is a kite with $AB = AD$ and $CB = CD$. $B\hat{A}D = {=p}^\circ$ and $B\hat{C}D = {=q}^\circ$. Calculate the size of $A\hat{B}C$, in degrees.
solution: The equal sides meet at $A$ (where $AB = AD$) and at $C$ (where $CB = CD$). The angles at $B$ and $D$ are the pair of opposite angles of the kite that are equal, so $A\hat{D}C = A\hat{B}C$.
The interior angles of a quadrilateral add up to $360^\circ$: $B\hat{A}D + A\hat{B}C + B\hat{C}D + A\hat{D}C = 360^\circ$.
Replace $A\hat{D}C$ by $A\hat{B}C$: ${=p}^\circ + 2 \times A\hat{B}C + {=q}^\circ = 360^\circ$, so $2 \times A\hat{B}C = 360^\circ - {=p}^\circ - {=q}^\circ = {=360 - p - q}^\circ$.
notes: Standard: the book's property 'one pair of opposite angles equal' plus the 360 degree angle sum of a quadrilateral. Diagram-free: the kite is fixed by naming AB = AD and CB = CD, so the equal angles are B and D. p + q is forced even so B is a whole number; p != q keeps the kite from being a rhombus; all four angles stay below 180 so the kite is convex. No mcq: both catalogued misconceptions are true/false judgements already covered by the book's basic questions.
